newsitem.title: FRANCE: Premiere expects two mln subscribers by mid-1998.
newsitem.headline: Premiere expects two mln subscribers by mid-1998.

text.p: German pay television group Premiere aims to have two million subscribers by the middle of 1998, Ewald Walgenbach, deputy managing director of CLT-UFA, the broadcasting division of Bertelsmann, said.
Walgenbach was speaking at a news conference at the MIP television trade fair in Cannes over the weekend.
The channel, 37.5 percent-owned each by Bertelsmann and France's Canal Plus with the remainder held by Bavarian media magnate Leo Kirch, currently counts some 1.4 million subscribers.
"Premiere's objective is to reach two million subscribers by the middle of next year," Walgenbach said.
CLT in January merged with Bertelsmann's UFA to create Europe's largest broadcasting group.
"CLT-UFA is the biggest buyer of programmes from American producers," Walgenbach said, adding the division spends three billion marks a year on buying programmes.
